title: Mixed forwarding deployments and where they break

prose.text: Most tenants mix methods, and the combinations fail in specific ways.

prose.label: Tunnels and Client Connector.
prose.text: {{gre-ztunnel2-egress}} The Client Connector and tunnel designs are in [[zia.traffic-forwarding.zcc]] and [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre]].

prose.label: PAC users on a tunnel site.
prose.text: {{pac-users-fall-to-other}} Sublocations are in [[zia.locations.sublocations]], and PAC forwarding is in [[zia.traffic-forwarding.pac]].

prose.label: Rules that depend on the path.
prose.text: SSL Inspection rules scoped by the CONNECT User-Agent match only explicit-mode traffic and never tunnel traffic: [[zia.ssl-inspection.criteria]]. Rules that need a user need Client Connector or Surrogate IP: [[zia.ssl-inspection.pipeline]], [[zia.authentication.unauthenticated-traffic]].

Dynamic Location Groups catching the wrong methods is open {{gap:location-group-mixing}}, and whether each method creates its own Location is open {{gap:location-per-method-mixed}}. Group behavior in general is [[zia.locations.groups]].

checks.do: Which methods carry which users at each site.
What the unmatched-address (other) sublocation rules would do to PAC traffic that was not planned for.
Whether the egress uses several GRE tunnels or ECMP, when a device shows Z-Tunnel 1.0 unexpectedly.

gre-ztunnel2-egress.statement: A site whose egress uses several GRE tunnels with different public source IPs, or ECMP, can present one device's Z-Tunnel 2.0 control and data connections from different IPs; per the vendor that splits them across Service Edges and Z-Tunnel 2.0 falls back to 1.0.
gre-ztunnel2-egress.conditions: The single-IP requirement and the fallback are stated by the vendor; that a multi-tunnel or ECMP GRE egress produces more than one source IP for one device's connections is the inference, and no source observes it.

pac-users-fall-to-other.statement: When a location has sublocations, PAC-forwarded traffic from users on that site is not matched to a sublocation unless XFF supplies the inner address, so it can land in the `other` sublocation and take whatever policy reaches it.
pac-users-fall-to-other.conditions: Both parts are stated separately (PAC loses internal IP visibility and sublocation policy; unmatched addresses go to `other`); that PAC traffic is placed in `other` is the combination and is not observed.

location-group-mixing.title: Dynamic Location Groups catching the wrong methods in mixed deployments
location-group-mixing.detail: Unverified legacy statement: A dynamic Location Group requiring SSL Inspection on may match both GRE locations and ZCC-equivalent implicit locations, so the group's attribute conditions must be specific. No captured source states it; a lab test would settle it.

location-per-method-mixed.title: Each method creating its own Location in a mixed tenant
location-per-method-mixed.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Each method creates a separate Location, or shares one through Surrogate IP for PAC users. No captured source states it; Zscaler Support or a vendor article would settle it.
